newsitem.title: USA: NYSE program trading 14.1 pct of volume Aug 26-30.
newsitem.headline: NYSE program trading 14.1 pct of volume Aug 26-30.

text.p: The New York Stock Exchange said program trading averaged 14.1 percent of its average daily volume of 293.4 million shares, or 41.4 million shares, for the week of August 26 through August 30.
Program trading accounted for an average of 9.0 percent of average daily volume of 328.3 million shares for the week of August 26-30.
Of the average 41.4 million shares during the week, buy programs accounted for an average 10.0 million shares, while sell programs accounted for an average 31.4 million daily.
In all markets, program trading averaged 62.3 million shares a day during the week of August 26-30.

Of the five member firms reporting the most program activity on the New York Stock Exchange, Morgan Stanley, First Boston and Nomura Securities conducted most of their program activity for their own accounts. First Options and Interactive Brokers executed all or most of their program activity for customers.

Program trading executed by firms as agent, for non-member customers, amounted to 56.3 percent during the week, while volume executed as principal, for their own accounts, amounted to 41.3 percent of program volume from August 26 through August 30.
During the week, 33.2 percent of program trading volume executed by NYSE member firms was related to index arbitrage, while another 19.7 percent involved other derivative product-related strategies.
Program trading encompasses trading strategies involving the sale or purchase of a basket of at least 15 stocks with a value of $1 million or more the exchange said.
